If the opponent correctly targets Politoed, it likely faints before singing, but Swampert-Mega enters for free with rain and Swift Swim active, outspeeding Staraptor next turn. Either branch advances the win condition better than passive double Protect or risky attacks that funnel both foe attacks into one slot.

decisions.rationale: Swampert-Mega is my last Pokémon at 14% HP. Both foes OHKO it: Staraptor Close Combat (47.5-66.7%), Dual Wingbeat (31.6-45.2%), and Kingambit Sucker Punch (38.4-54.8%) or Kowtow Cleave (46.3-66.1%) all guarantee the KO. If I attack, Kingambit's +1 priority Sucker Punch KOs me before I move. Protect (+4 priority) goes first and blocks both foes. Second consecutive Protect has ~50% success rate, which is slim but strictly better than the 0% from forfeiting or attacking. No single attack KOs both foes (Staraptor immune to Earthquake), and even a crit Wave Crash OHKO on Staraptor leaves Kingambit to KO me. The position is nearly hopeless, but Protect preserves the only non-zero path: multiple Protect successes plus crits or opponent misplay.
decisions.notebook: Game 2, down 0-1. Rain mode with Swampert-Mega Swift Swim was primary win condition. Staraptor-Mega Contrary at +5/+5 is nearly unbreakable without critical hits. Politoed (Perish Song) fainted, so no Perish Song counter remains. All other teammates fainted. Swampert-Mega is last mon standing at low HP against two healthy foes with priority Sucker Punch. Only multiple consecutive Protect successes plus critical hits could theoretically win; position is effectively lost.

decisions.rationale: Both attackers guarantee KO on 13% Swampert-Mega (Close Combat 34.8-60%, Sucker Punch 29-51.4%, Dual Wingbeat 24.2-41.1%). Swampert outspeeds Staraptor 180-244 vs 178 in Rain with Swift Swim, and Wave Crash guarantees KO on Kingambit 65.7-91.8% if it moves first. Sucker Punch priority +1 KOs Swampert before it can attack if it chooses Wave Crash/Earthquake/Ice Punch, securing immediate game win since Swampert is last alive foe. Close Combat is 100% accurate vs Dual Wingbeat 90% and also KO's even if Sucker Punch is wasted by a successful Protect (33% on consecutive Protect), with Staraptor surviving any hit (Ice Punch 14.1-20.5%, Wave Crash 24.9-34.6% with +5 Def/SpD).

reflections.summary: Won Game 2 to close series 2-0 with clean piloting (0 errors) and a favorable preview plan. Preview: Staraptor-Mega/Farigiraf/Kingambit/Arcanine-Hisui correctly answered opponent's Rain Perish/Hypnosis core (Politoed/Swampert-Mega/Kommo-o/Vivillon-Tundra) - Mega Staraptor was the only Mega to evolve and Contrary Close Combat was ideal vs physical Swift Swim + Soundproof Kommo-o, Flying immunity blanked Swampert EQ, Farigiraf Armor Tail + Protect denied Hypnosis/Perish pressure, Kingambit Life Orb Sucker Punch covered Gengar-Mega trap even though it was benched. Piloting: stacked +5 Def/SpD on Staraptor via repeated Close Combats into Politoed/Kommo-o/Vivillon, used Protect to block Hypnosis (T1,T4) and focused Politoed early to remove Drizzle/Weather Ball/Perish enabler and prevent rain reset, removed Sash Vivillon before Rage Powder value, and preserved boosted Staraptor + Kingambit endgame vs low Swampert. Between-game adjustments held - no backfire, same Contrary pressure plan that won G1 continued to deny the Rain trap in G2.
reflections.adjustment: No overhaul needed after 2-0, but expect the benched Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag Perish + Incineroar Intimidate/Fake Out variant next series - keep Kingambit Sucker Punch and Farigiraf Protect/Armor Tail, keep leading Staraptor to stack Contrary early but add earlier pressure on Politoed to avoid Hypnosis sleep turns and keep Tailwind/Protect option ready if they pivot to Perish trap instead of pure Rain Hypnosis.

reflections.summary: The series was lost 0-2 primarily because we had no reliable answer to Contrary Staraptor-Mega, which accumulated multiple defense boosts from Close Combat and became unbreakable. In game 2, we failed to use Swampert's Ice Punch (super effective) against it, instead relying on neutral hits and sleep, which were insufficient. Politoed was lost early, preventing Perish Song. Our rain mode was out-sustained by Staraptor's snowballing bulk.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, lead with Politoed and Swampert to immediately threaten Staraptor with rain-boosted Swift Swim Ice Punch before it can boost. Preserve Politoed for Perish Song as a fallback. Consider bringing Raichu over Vivillon for Fake Out pressure and a special Mega that can bypass defense boosts, or use Kommo-o's Clanging Scales early to chip both foes. Always respect Kingambit's Sucker Punch in endgames by keeping Protect available.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's Staraptor-Mega has Contrary; it will aggressively use Close Combat to raise both defenses. It often leads with Farigiraf (Trick Room/Helping Hand) and pairs with Kingambit (Life Orb, Sucker Punch, Swords Dance) and Arcanine-Hisui (Rock Head, Focus Sash). Farigiraf may attempt Trick Room; deny it or exploit the sleep we landed. Swampert-Mega's Ice Punch is our best immediate answer to Staraptor; use it early before boosts accumulate. Politoed's Perish Song is a win condition if Staraptor becomes too bulky. Kingambit's Sucker Punch can be played around with Protect or faster moves. Avoid bringing Vivillon if Staraptor is present, as Dual Wingbeat ignores Focus Sash.
